item.title: National Democrats pour $7.5M into Florida races ahead of November election
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: National Democratic groups are significantly increasing their financial commitments to Florida's competitive races as the November election approaches, according to a statement from the Florida Democratic Party. The Democratic Attorneys General Association announced a $5 million investment supporting José Javier Rodríguez's campaign for Florida…
item.content:encoded:
National Democratic groups are significantly increasing their financial commitments to Florida's competitive races as the November election approaches, according to a statement from the Florida Democratic Party.

The Democratic Attorneys General Association announced a $5 million investment supporting José Javier Rodríguez's campaign for Florida Attorney General, while the Democratic super PAC American Bridge has spent $2.5 million in Florida's U.S. Senate race as part of a broader nationwide effort. Together, the commitments total at least $7.5 million in new resources flowing into the state.

Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried characterized the national investment as validation of grassroots organizing work in the state. "National Democrats are putting real money behind Florida because they see what we've been building on the ground for the last three years," Fried said in a statement, citing recruitment of more than 1,000 candidates and efforts to flip competitive seats.

The investments underscore how Florida has become a focal point for both parties in the lead-up to November's general election, with national organizations viewing several races in the state as competitive and potentially winnable.

item.content:encoded:
A Florida Department of Children and Families Comfort Center has opened in Century to help residents recovering from hurricane damage. The facility, located at the Century Business Center at 150 East Pond Street, is distributing essential supplies at no cost, including food, diapers, feminine hygiene products, tarps, and cleaning materials.

The center also operates 24/7 shower and laundry trailers on site, providing critical services for residents whose homes may lack running water or functional utilities following the storm. The relief effort is part of DCF's broader disaster response network across the state.

Residents in need can visit the center during operating hours. The availability of these basic services reflects the ongoing recovery challenges many North Escambia families face as they work to restore their homes and lives.

item.title: 120,000 gallons of sewage overflow near Century lift station
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: An estimated 120,000 gallons of untreated sewage spilled near Century after a temporary bypass pump became overwhelmed by a surge of wastewater, according to an initial pollution report filed with the state. The Town of Century reported the spill occurred at the prison lift station on Tedder Road, just off North Century Boulevard. Lift stations…
item.content:encoded:
An estimated 120,000 gallons of untreated sewage spilled near Century after a temporary bypass pump became overwhelmed by a surge of wastewater, according to an initial pollution report filed with the state. The Town of Century reported the spill occurred at the prison lift station on Tedder Road, just off North Century Boulevard.

Lift stations are critical infrastructure that pump wastewater uphill to treatment facilities. The temporary bypass pump was apparently in use as a workaround when the main system couldn't handle the volume of incoming sewage.

The state has been notified of the spill through the required pollution reporting process. Details on the cause of the surge, environmental impact, or remediation efforts were not immediately available.

item.content:encoded: The Salvation Army is providing free meals at multiple locations across Escambia County on Monday, offering both lunch and dinner to residents in need. Boxed lunches will be available around noon, followed by hot dinners at approximately 5:30 p.m. at two confirmed sites: Carver Park Resource Center at 208 Webb Street in Cantonment and the Old Century High Gym at 720 East Hecker Road in Century, which is slated to become a future community shelter. The meal service is part of the Salvation Army's ongoing community support efforts in the county. Residents looking for additional details about the program or other meal distribution sites can contact the Salvation Army directly.

item.content:encoded:
Team Rubicon Disaster Response, a nationwide volunteer organization, has mobilized crews to help communities across Northwest Florida bounce back from Hurricane Isaias, according to WKRG News 5.

The volunteers, who traveled to the region from across the country, are working in areas including Milton and surrounding communities affected by the storm. Team Rubicon specializes in rapid-response disaster recovery, coordinating skilled volunteers to assist with cleanup, repair, and rebuilding efforts in the aftermath of major weather events.

The effort marks part of the broader recovery operation underway across the Panhandle as residents and local organizations work to clear debris, restore utilities, and repair homes and infrastructure damaged by the hurricane.

item.title: FPL Mobilizes 5,000 Crews Across 29 States to Restore Power to 332,000 Panhandle Customers
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The utility has mobilized approximately 5,000 restoration workers from 29 states to accelerate recovery efforts in the region. The scale of the outage and…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Power & Light has deployed crews from across the nation to restore electricity to more than 332,000 customers in the Panhandle following what appears to be a significant weather event. The utility has mobilized approximately 5,000 restoration workers from 29 states to accelerate recovery efforts in the region.

The scale of the outage and multi-state response suggests a major weather system impacted the area. Escambia County residents and businesses across the Panhandle remain without power as crews work to repair infrastructure and reconnect service.

FPL has not yet provided an estimated timeline for full restoration, though the company's mobilization of such a large workforce indicates the utility is treating the situation with urgency. Customers experiencing outages are advised to check FPL's website or contact the utility for updates on service restoration in their specific areas.

item.title: Santa Rosa Sheriff warns of scammers targeting Hurricane Isaias victims

Scammers often target disaster victims by posing as contractors, insurance adjusters, or relief workers seeking payment for cleanup, repairs, or assistance. Residents should verify the legitimacy…
item.content:encoded:
The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office is alerting residents to be on guard against fraudsters attempting to exploit people affected by Hurricane Isaias.

Scammers often target disaster victims by posing as contractors, insurance adjusters, or relief workers seeking payment for cleanup, repairs, or assistance. Residents should verify the legitimacy of anyone requesting money or personal information before providing either.

The Sheriff's Office advises victims to work only with licensed contractors, check credentials carefully, and report suspicious activity to local law enforcement. More details on common hurricane-related scams and how to protect yourself are available through the Sheriff's Office.

item.title: DOH-Santa Rosa Reopening Limited Services Wednesday After Weather
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will partially reopen Wednesday following severe weather that forced closures, according to a statement from the health department's public information office. Only two offices will resume operations with limited hours: the Women, Infant, and Children (WIC) office will be open from 7:30 a.m. to…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will partially reopen Wednesday following severe weather that forced closures, according to a statement from the health department's public information office.

Only two offices will resume operations with limited hours: the Women, Infant, and Children (WIC) office will be open from 7:30 a.m. to noon, and the Vital Statistics office will operate from 8 a.m. to noon, both in Milton.

The health department says hours and services for Thursday and Friday will be announced in a separate update. Residents needing more information can call DOH-Santa Rosa at 850-983-5200.

item.title: Santa Rosa Health Department Partially Reopens Wednesday After Storm
item.dc:creator: newsroom

Beginning Wednesday, October 14, only the Women, Infant, and Children (WIC) office and Vital Statistics office in Milton will be open. The WIC office will operate from 7:30 a.m. to noon, while Vital…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will resume limited operations this week following severe weather that forced closures. Beginning Wednesday, October 14, only the Women, Infant, and Children (WIC) office and Vital Statistics office in Milton will be open.

The WIC office will operate from 7:30 a.m. to noon, while Vital Statistics will be available from 8 a.m. to noon on Wednesday. The health department said it will release updated hours and service information for Thursday and Friday in a separate announcement.

Residents needing to reach the department can call 850-983-5200 for more details. The partial reopening represents the first step toward full restoration of services at the Santa Rosa County health offices.

item.title: Pensacola Day 4: Power restored to 97K as cleanup continues
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As Pensacola enters its fourth day of recovery from Hurricane Isaias, city crews are maintaining round-the-clock efforts to clear debris and restore critical services, according to an 11 a.m. update from the City of Pensacola Public Information Office. Florida Power & Light has restored electricity to approximately 97,000 customers across Escambia…
item.content:encoded:
As Pensacola enters its fourth day of recovery from Hurricane Isaias, city crews are maintaining round-the-clock efforts to clear debris and restore critical services, according to an 11 a.m. update from the City of Pensacola Public Information Office.

Florida Power & Light has restored electricity to approximately 97,000 customers across Escambia County as of Monday morning. City officials are urging residents to remain cautious as downed trees, power lines, and other storm hazards remain scattered throughout the area.

"Our crews have been working nonstop, pitching in wherever they are needed," the city said in its update. "They're tired. You're tired. But remember this is a marathon, not a sprint." The focus remains on public safety, debris removal, and restoring critical infrastructure and services to the community.

The storm's impact on Santa Rosa County schools underscores the region's vulnerability to major hurricanes and highlights the need for continued preparedness and resilience planning among local institutions.
